The first meeting of the RPSB took place at Ike's Shrimp House on October 23, 1969, with Mr. P.S. Jones former chairman of VOICES presiding. Two volunteer committees, the nominating committee and the by-laws committee were organized with one representative from each district.
In December, 1969, the Department of Housing and Urban Development announced the funding of the Randolph Conservation Program.
After months of work the Board met at the West End RCAP Center on January 6, 1970, and elected, by ballot, a slate of officers. Officers included Mr. Petronius S. Jones, Chairman; Mr. Herbert Johnson, Vice Chairman; Mrs. Wilnette Branch, Recording Secretary; Mrs. Wilhelen Satterwhite, Corresponding Secretary; Reverend Nathaniel Winston, Chaplin; Reverend Raymond Mitchell, Parlimentarian; and Mr. Steven Gary, Treasurer. The Board also ratified a constitution and by-laws.
During the following months the RPSB conducted a series of sessions held at the West End RCAP Center to inform community people of the urban renewal program and get their involvement and input into the program. At the same time, Mr. Robert Everton, Director of Redevelopment (RRHA), Mr. John Baker, RRHA, Mr. Fred N. Thomas, Director off Community Relations (RRHA) and Mr. Alan Siff, Consultant Planner (Harland Bartholomew and Associates) conducted educational sessions with the PAC members and community about the urban renewal program.
Since its creation the Randolph Planning Study Board has worked very hard to insure that the Renewal Plan for this area will reflect the thinking and desires of the people of the entire project area. Each of the six project area districts has organized and meets at least once a month to discuss the progress of the renewal efforts, to receive suggestions from any interested parties and to insure an opportunity for participation from all community citizens. The elected representatives from all districts meet at least once a month to discuss and coordinate the ideas and comments throughout the area. Meetings have been held by the Board to inform the community as a whole of the progress of the renewal effort and to answer questions pertinent to renewal in Randolph.
Board members first established a time schedule of all the Randolph Planning Study Board functions and activities. All of the scheduled activities have not been completed on time, but an orderly sequence of activities has resulted in much more efficient use of time than might normally be expected.
In August of 1970, Mr. C. Bernard Gilpin was employed as project director and a joint site office of the RPSB and RRHA was established at 1610 Winder Street. RRHA also provided a community relations assistant to work with the PAC to achieve its goal of maximum citizen participation. In that same month RPSB received approval for an operating budget.
The Randolph Planning Study Board members began by analyzing and identifying the physical problems of their community. They conducted blight surveys and environmental surveys on a district by district basis and compared their findings with those of their consultants. Community representatives comprised an integral part of the teams which conducted the "Typical" surveys required by the federal application for renewal funds. A special committee of the Randolph Planning Study Board with the assistance of its architectural consultant has produced the Residential Rehabilitation Standards, also to be included as part of the total proposal. Another special committee worked with planning consultants to study proposed and uses for the area.
